ai_insights.executive_summary: During the 180‑second test with 20 concurrent users, 2,976 requests were processed at an aggregate throughput of 16.53 req/s, but 31.58% resulted in errors. Overall SLA compliance was 73.6%, with 64 transactions exceeding their response‑time or error‑rate targets. Server CPU peaked at 91.4% and memory at 89.3%, indicating severe infrastructure saturation.

findings.title: Server CPU Saturation at Peak Concurrency
findings.observation: CPU utilization rose from 34% at start to a peak of 91.4% at 20 concurrent users, with average CPU of 60.7% across the run. This saturated state coincided with the highest P95 latency of 2,446 ms and a throughput drop to 1.9 req/s in the final interval.
findings.likely_cause: Insufficient CPU capacity relative to concurrent request load, causing thread queuing and increased processing delays.
findings.why_it_matters: High CPU utilization leads to increased response times, transaction timeouts, and elevated error rates, directly impacting user experience and SLA compliance.
findings.recommendation: Scale out the application tier by adding additional instances or increasing instance size to keep CPU below 80% under peak load.
findings.validation: Re‑run the test with increased CPU resources; expect CPU peak <80% and P95 latency to fall below 1,000 ms.

findings.title: Memory Utilization Approaching Capacity
findings.observation: Memory usage climbed to 89.3% peak, with average 69.3%. High memory consumption correlates with increased garbage collection activity and latency spikes.
findings.likely_cause: Memory leak or insufficient heap allocation causing frequent garbage collection and swapping.
findings.why_it_matters: Memory pressure can cause application pauses, increased latency, and potential OutOfMemory errors, further degrading performance.
findings.recommendation: Increase allocated memory or tune JVM heap parameters; monitor GC pauses.
findings.validation: After tuning, observe memory peak <80% and reduced GC pause times.

findings.title: High Rate of Server‑Side HTTP Errors
findings.observation: Azure App Service recorded 168 HTTP 5xx errors and 80 HTTP 404 errors, resulting in a 100% error rate for 17 distinct transactions.
findings.likely_cause: Application exceptions and missing endpoints under load, possibly due to resource exhaustion or unhandled exceptions.
findings.why_it_matters: These errors cause complete transaction failures, directly violating the 1% error rate SLA and causing a 31.58% overall error rate.
findings.recommendation: Implement robust error handling, add retry logic, and ensure all endpoints are properly deployed and resilient to load.
findings.validation: After fixes, error rate should drop below 1% for affected transactions.

findings.title: Critical Transactions Exceed Response Time SLAs
findings.observation: Transaction TC01_T_01_Launch_Homepage had a P90 of 1,181 ms against a 250 ms target (+372% deviation). TC02_T_05_Add_Bulldog_To_Cart P90 706 ms vs 600 ms target (+17.7%). TC02_T_09_Update_Cart_Quantities P90 676 ms vs 600 ms target (+12.7%). These breaches contributed to 64 SLA‑violating transactions.
findings.likely_cause: Inefficient backend queries and contention on shared resources during peak load.
findings.why_it_matters: Breaching response time SLAs results in poor user experience and potential contractual penalties.
findings.recommendation: Optimize database queries, add caching, and consider asynchronous processing for these hot paths.
findings.validation: Post‑optimization, verify P90 values meet target thresholds.

findings.title: Throughput Plateau and Late‑Stage Degradation
findings.observation: Throughput rose to 3.7 req/s at 1m20s then declined to 1.9 req/s by 3m, while latency increased from 702 ms to 672 ms average but P95 remained high (830 ms). Error count remained steady at 5‑14 per interval.
findings.likely_cause: System reaching maximum concurrency limits, causing request queueing and increased latency.
findings.why_it_matters: Reduced throughput under sustained load indicates inability to scale, leading to potential request timeouts.
findings.recommendation: Implement horizontal scaling with auto‑scale rules to add instances when CPU or latency thresholds are exceeded.
findings.validation: After scaling, throughput should sustain >3.5 req/s without degradation.

capacity_planning.saturation_point: At 20 concurrent users, CPU reached 91.4% and latency spiked, indicating saturation at this concurrency.
capacity_planning.analysis: The system exhibited linear throughput growth up to ~3.5 req/s, then plateaued and declined as CPU and memory approached maximum. This suggests the current instance size is insufficient for more than 20 simultaneous users.

custom_edits.summary_html: CONDITIONAL GO: Average response time improved 25% (398ms to 299ms) and SLA pass rate rose 8.3pp year-over-year. However, TC03_T_01_Launch_Search_Portal p95 tail latency regressed from 1339ms to 2163ms, crossing the 1500ms SLA threshold and representing the primary bottleneck driver. Overall error rate remained flat at ~11%, confirming the release is viable with targeted tail latency mitigation.
custom_edits.highlights_html:
• Average response time across all percentiles dropped 25% (p99: 1454ms to 1148ms), driven by reduced processing overhead in the current test execution.
  • SLA pass rate improved from 29.2% to 37.5%, primarily due to latency compression in transactions with tight SLA targets (e.g., TC01_T_03, TC02_T_06, TC01_T_06 now passing where baseline breached).
  • TC03_T_01_Launch_Search_Portal p95 tail latency spiked from 1339ms to 2163ms, crossing the 1500ms SLA threshold and representing the most significant regression in this release.
  • Error rate held steady at ~11% across both runs, indicating the latency improvements did not introduce new reliability risks but also did not resolve the underlying error source.
custom_edits.recommendations_html:
• [Database / Indexing]: Optimize search portal query paths and add targeted indexes to suppress p95 tail latency below 1500ms SLA threshold.
  • [Application Gateway / Thread Pool]: Audit and rebalance thread pool sizing and connection pool saturation points responsible for the persistent ~11% error rate across authentication and checkout transactions.

- **Transaction Failure Dichotomy**: While 5 transactions (TC01_T_01_Launch_Homepage, TC03_T_01_Launch_Search_Portal, etc.) failed with 100% error rate but high latency (avg 901-974ms), another set of 5 transactions (TC03_T_01_R_02_GET_Search_Bar_Widget, TC01_T_01_R_03_GET_Banner_Logo, etc.) failed with 100% error rate but extremely low latency (avg 162-165ms), indicating two distinct failure modes: timeout-induced slowness versus immediate connection/application errors.
  
- **Network Behavior During Peak Load**: At the exact CPU peak timestamp (2026-08-10T00:20:00Z), network input was 71.53 Mbps and output 45.78 Mbps—both *lower* than the values 5 minutes prior (81.7 Mbps in, 56.01 Mbps out at 2026-08-10T00:15:00Z)—confirming the bottleneck was CPU-bound processing saturation, not network bandwidth exhaustion.

- **Memory Persistence Post-Peak**: After CPU peaked at 91.4% (00:20Z), it decreased to 68.2% by 00:25Z, but memory remained elevated at 82.7% (vs. 89.3% peak), suggesting potential memory leak or insufficient garbage collection as load decreased, which could impair recovery.

- **Iteration-to-Sample Discrepancy**: With 15 total iterations but 15 samples per transaction (e.g., TC04_T_01_Launch_Authentication_Gateway: samples=15, iterations=0), the test design appears to execute exactly one sample of each transaction per iteration—indicating minimal think time or pacing between requests, maximizing sustained load on the server.

- **Tail Latency Severity**: The overall P99 response time (1148ms) was 6.3x higher than the P50 (167ms), revealing extreme response time variability where the slowest 1% of requests experienced over 1 second of latency despite median performance being sub-300ms.
